- Peet’s: Bold, darker roasts; better straight espresso and pour-overs (US West/online).
- Blue Bottle: Lighter, specialty coffee; great espresso and drip, minimal sweet drinks (major cities).
- Dutch Bros: Drive-thru focused, super friendly, lots of sweet/energy-style drinks (US West).
- Caribou Coffee: Cozy vibe, solid mochas and blended drinks (Midwest US + some intl).
- Philz: Custom pour-overs by the cup; no espresso drinks (select US cities).
- Tim Hortons: Affordable coffee and donuts, huge in Canada, expanding in US/UK/Gulf.
- Costa Coffee or Caffè Nero: Reliable choices across the UK/Europe.
- Pret a Manger: Good filter coffee and quick fresh food (UK, US cities, Europe).

Tell me your location and what you prefer (espresso vs. sweet drinks, study spot vs. drive-thru, budget, non-dairy), and I’ll narrow it to the best fit.

Short answer: you can’t go wrong with Sony or Canon for a versatile, future‑proof system. If you like classic controls and APS‑C, look at Fujifilm. For video, Panasonic is great. For travel/wildlife and stabilization, OM System is strong. For stills ergonomics and image quality value, Nikon shines.

Quick brand guide:
- Sony (E‑mount): Best all‑rounder. Class‑leading autofocus, huge native and third‑party lens selection, strong stills and video.
- Canon (RF): Great ergonomics, color, autofocus, and lenses. Third‑party RF autofocus lenses are more limited.
- Nikon (Z): Excellent image quality and dynamic range, comfortable bodies, superb native lenses; third‑party support is growing.
- Fujifilm (X): APS‑C with tactile dials, great JPEG color/film simulations, compact high‑quality primes.
- Panasonic (S and Micro Four Thirds): Video‑first features, good value; S5‑series for full‑frame video, G/GH lines for MFT.
- OM System (Micro Four Thirds): Best‑in‑class stabilization, lightweight kits, great for travel, wildlife, and long reach.
- Pentax/Ricoh (DSLR): Rugged, weather‑sealed, optical viewfinders; niche but beloved by DSLR purists.
- Leica: Premium build and rangefinder experience; niche and expensive.

If you share:
- Budget
- What you mostly shoot (travel, portraits, sports, wildlife, video, low‑light, etc.)
- Size/weight preference
- Any must‑have features (IBIS, weather sealing, viewfinder, 4K/slow‑mo)

…I’ll narrow it to 1–2 brands and a few specific models to match.
